 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. In this story Tanner McKee is tasked with steadying the Eagles' ship for at least the next month. And the waters around Philadelphia are getting pretty rocky these days.
 Jalen Hurts being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot that puts him on injured reserve is the latest in a deepening injury problem, ruling the quarterback out for Sunday's game against the Panthers and for at least three games after that. The timing couldn't be worse with the Eagles having lost three straight, the past two in heartbreaking fashion.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement McKee was named Hurts' replacement. Andy Dalton had been Hurts' backup to open the season but was cut after an interception against the Bears in Week 3.
 McKee has started two career games, both coming in meaningless Week 18 games. Last season, after the Eagles had clinched a playoff spot the week before, McKee completed 21-of-40 passes for 241 yards, one TD and one interception in the 24-17 loss to the Commanders.
 The Eagles listed 24 players on this week's injury report , not to mention the five offensive players on injured reserve. The offensive line also took recent hits with the sudden retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson and the trade of left guard Cam Jurgens. 
 McKee will be the starting quarterback during a key stretch of the Eagles' season. After the Panthers, the Eagles face each of their NFC East rivals leading into the Week 10 bye — Monday night against the Cowboys, at the Commanders and home against the division-leading Giants.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Can McKee offer the 2-3 Eagles any hope? And if not, how might they handle the back half of the season if things continue to go awry?
 McKee's challenges with a limited Eagles offense
 The Eagles' offense will look very different with McKee at QB. Where Hurts can use his mobility to make plays, that's not McKee's game at all. He's a pocket-passer through and through. His 13 career rushing attempts include multiple kneeldowns.
 That also factors into his pocket mobility, which hasn't been a strong suit. McKee took three sacks in his Week 18 start last season and two in his 2024 start against the Giants. It was a consistent knock against him in college.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That figures to be a concern given the shape of the Eagles' offensive line. In addition to losing two starters, the Eagles are currently monitoring the health of center Drew Kendall (knee), who returned to practice after missing Week 5. Tyler Steen was limited with a shoulder injury. Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, but his 21-day practice window opened this week.
 On the good-news front, injury-wise, wide receiver DeVonta Smith practiced for the first time in a few weeks. But there was far more bad news. Running backs Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Will Shipley (foot) didn't practice for a second straight day, and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks was downgraded from limited Wednesday to "did not practice" on Thursday with a hamstring injury.
 With Tank Bigsby on IR, the running back room could be down to Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. That puts the run game in a scary place if Barkley and Shipley can't go, which would put McKee even more in the crosshairs. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has praised McKee's ability to put the ball in the right place and knowing where to go with the rock. McKee's one interception in 88 NFL pass attempts appears to back up that assertion. But Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion are going to have to come up with a clever script to mask their weaknesses and play to McKee's strengths with a system that's meant to marry the pass to the run game.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If there's a potential bright side, it's perhaps that McKee might have more chemistry with some of the Eagles' offensive reserves who might be thrust into bigger roles. And if ever there's a time for Mannion to put on his former QB2 hat and cook up a killer menu, Sunday is the time.
 This is a big challenge for McKee and the Eagles.
 Could the Eagles quickly become sellers?
 The Eagles have been theoretical and practical buyers at the trade deadline in just about every year Sirianni has been coach. (The only year they didn't make a regular-season trade prior to the deadline was in 2024, although they had made a preseason trade for Jahan Dotson that year.) 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement And the Eagles can't just punt on the season now. The division is in wretched shape, with three of the four teams facing QB injury concerns and all four facing major questions currently. One of those four teams will win the East, however, and the Eagles — division winners three of the past four years and currently 1-0 in division games — arguably have as good a shot as any of them.
 But if they lost to Carolina and dropped two or three more before the bye, they'd be staring at 2-7 or 3-6 at the bye. Even a 4-5 record might not mean much if Hurts' outlook isn't great after missing these next four games. And yes, winning the division a third straight time would be something, but how much potential does this version of the Eagles really have?
 Philadelphia's bye starts Nov. 9. The trade deadline is the next day. It would not be a shock to see the Eagles become deadline sellers for the first time in many years.
 The Jurgens trade was the first sale, and a curious one. Did that not tip general manager Howie Roseman's hand slightly? The Eagles can talk in whatever circles they want to about the trade, but the timing was beyond interesting.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement They have several players who could be moved. Dickerson might be gone next offseason, so you'd have to think he'd be available if someone wanted him. Nolan Smith feels like a pricy third rusher. Moro Ojomo might be a goner in free agency, so you might as well field offers now. You could even make a case for dangling Barkley, if the price was right and the Eagles were far enough out of contention.
 The Eagles have been stockpiling picks for the next two drafts, and it makes sense that Roseman would want to continue doing so. Hurts is also entering a critical stage of his career, with 2027 perhaps a critical season to determine his place with the franchise.
 Right now, Hurts is shelved. And with this season already headed in the wrong direction, it would make sense to consider tacking against the wind.
